package_info.why_malicious: Multiple vulnerabilities in BusyBox applets allow attackers to trigger denial of service, information leaks, and potentially remote code execution by supplying crafted input to affected utilities. The vulnerabilities stem from improper input validation, use-after-free, and out-of-bounds memory access, making the package dangerous when exposed to untrusted data.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when decompressing LZMA data via unlzma, unzip, tar, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when decompressing a crafted LZMA stream, the code calculates a buffer offset using attacker-controlled values, leading to an out-of-bounds read from memory, which is then written to the decompressed output, resulting in information leakage.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code uses attacker-controlled values (dict_size, rep0) to calculate a buffer offset without sufficient bounds checking, allowing out-of-bounds memory access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal decompression should only access memory within the allocated buffer; here, the code can read arbitrary memory locations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate decompression routines may use similar logic but must always enforce strict bounds checks.
key_indicators: Potential for information leak or crash

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when decompressing LZMA data via unlzma, unzip, tar, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code flushes the decompression buffer when it reaches the user-controlled dictionary size, resetting the buffer position to zero, which is a prerequisite for triggering the out-of-bounds read in the previous snippet.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The buffer flush is triggered by a user-controlled value (dict_size), which can be manipulated to set up the conditions for an out-of-bounds read.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Buffer management should not allow user input to control internal pointer resets in a way that enables memory safety violations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Buffer flushes are normal in decompression, but not when dictated by untrusted input.
key_indicators: Pointer reset based on attacker input

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when decompressing LZMA data via unlzma, unzip, tar, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes the potentially out-of-bounds match_byte, propagating leaked memory bits into the decompressed output, which can be extracted by an attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code uses a value (match_byte) that may have been read from an out-of-bounds memory location, further propagating the leak.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Decompression routines should not process or output memory outside the intended buffer.

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious LZMA-compressed file (or ZIP file with LZMA-compressed entry) with specific dictionary size and match parameters.
attack_chain.leads_to: File is supplied to a vulnerable BusyBox applet (unlzma, unzip, tar, etc.)

attack_chain.action: BusyBox applet decompresses the file, using attacker-controlled dictionary size to flush the buffer and reset buffer_pos to 0.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sets up conditions for out-of-bounds read

attack_chain.action: Decompression logic calculates a negative buffer offset using attacker-controlled rep0 and dict_size, resulting in an out-of-bounds read from memory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Leaked memory is read into match_byte

attack_chain.action: Leaked memory (match_byte) is processed and written to the decompressed output, which is then accessible to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker extracts leaked memory from output file

behavioral_signatures: Decompression of LZMA streams with unusually large or attacker-controlled dictionary sizes
BusyBox applets crashing (segmentation fault) when processing compressed files
Unexpected memory reads or information leaks during decompression
file_indicators: LZMA-compressed files with crafted headers (e.g., large dictionary size, specific match parameters)
ZIP files with LZMA-compressed entries (compression type 14)
network_indicators: N/A (attack is local, but exfiltration may occur if output is accessible remotely)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for BusyBox applet crashes (segfaults) when decompressing files, especially ZIP or LZMA files. Flag files with LZMA headers specifying unusually large dictionary sizes or crafted match parameters. Use static analysis to detect decompress_unlzma.c code paths where buffer offsets are calculated from user-controlled values without proper bounds checks. Consider sandboxing or restricting decompression of untrusted files on embedded devices.
